adopted.CLAUDE.md: adopted in full. This repo keeps no decision docs — docs/ holds plans and transient review artifacts only — and the source's § "Writing things down" routes a decision's alternatives to the PR or issue thread, which is what this repo already does. /audit-github-backlog carries the last upstream mention of decision docs, and it is declined. § "Language" is filled in rather than left as the source's adopter stub, and its § "Vetting" exit rule does not travel: that rule is about a stub over an unchecked stack, and this repo's vet.sh is real.

adopted..claude/skills/plainly/: adopted whole, operators.md included. The source marks that file `rewrite` because its one entry is its own operator's; here that is the same person, so there is nothing to re-derive. A second operator gets an entry of their own rather than a rewrite of this one.

adopted..claude/skills/update-muthur/: this skill, under the name it has there — the source has renamed it three times (sync-upstream, sync-agent-infra, sync-muthur, update-muthur) and ships it as an unhydrated stub. The local copy is /sync-muthur and its procedure is hydrated, so what lands from a commit touching this path is the procedure's own changes, never the stub framing or the name. The verb is where the two part: the source names the command for the tree it runs in, which is muthur there and this repo here, so `update` inverts one link down. The watermark filename is the source's own — watermark.json, what every downstream adopter has on disk — and nothing locates either by path anyway.

adopted..claude/skills/spinoff/: taken with three translations, none of which the closure check can see. Its § "The watermark" pointer is repointed at /sync-muthur. Its claim that the target's sync skill is named after the root holds here, so that paragraph stands as written but for the verb — /sync-muthur against the source's /update-muthur — which Step 1's find-by-contents rule already makes harmless. The relative link to the source's catalog.md resolves to nothing here and reads as any catalog.md under .claude/skills/. And the stackless-vet rule it cites as CLAUDE.md § "Vetting" is the source's clause, declined here, so the skill states it itself. Its catalog refusal needs no translation: this repo has no catalog, which is exactly the signal that says a caller may spin off.

adopted.scripts/vet.sh: rewritten for this stack: pnpm build alone and first (it regenerates .next/types/, which tsconfig includes), then styles:codegen alone, then the rest fanned out through run-parallel.sh. CLAUDE.md § Vetting carries the roster and why each check sits where it does. Read the source's edits for the idea; the file itself never lands.
